documentedSources.title: Set up staging environments in Azure App Service

claims.text: Deployment slots are available only in the Standard, Premium or Isolated tier of an App Service plan.
There is no extra charge for using deployment slots; the Standard tier supports only five slots.
Auto swap is not supported in web apps on Linux or in Web App for Containers.
To roll back a swap, swap the same two slots again immediately.
By default an instance that returns any HTTP response counts as warmed up; WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_PATH and WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_STATUSES make the check strict.
Former production instances are recycled in the last swap step and long-running operations on them are abandoned.
The target slot stays online while the source slot is prepared and warmed up, whether or not the swap succeeds.
Swap with preview applies the target slot settings to the source slot first; the swap can then be completed (CompleteSlotSwap) or cancelled (ResetSlotSwap).

documentedSources.title: Azure subscription and service limits: App Service limits

claims.text: Staging slots per app: none in Free, Shared and Basic; 5 in Standard; 20 in Premium; 20 in Isolated.
Testing in Production (slot traffic percentage) and Autoscale are available from Standard upward; Always On from Basic upward.
In the dedicated tiers (Basic, Standard, Premium, PremiumV2, PremiumV3, PremiumV4) each VM instance of the plan is charged.
All deployment slots of an app run on the same VM instances as the plan; an active slot competes for plan resources.
Deployment slots, custom domains, TLS certificates and backups are not charged as features; App Service domains, App Service certificates and IP-based TLS are exceptions.

documentedSources.title: Configure Node.js apps in Azure App Service

claims.text: On Linux the runtime is selected with az webapp config set --linux-fx-version "NODE|24-lts"; the page metadata shows updated_at 2026-10-19.
On Linux App Service sets the PORT environment variable and forwards requests to it; the app must listen on process.env.PORT.
Premium v4 is available for source code apps and custom containers on Linux, in select regions; the listed public regions include Central US, East US, East US 2, West US 2 and West US 3.
Premium v4 has no stable outbound IP addresses by design.
Premium v4 availability also depends on the underlying App Service deployment of the resource group and region combination.
Budget notifications are triggered when thresholds are exceeded; resources are not affected and consumption is not stopped.
Cost data is typically available within 8 to 24 hours and budgets are evaluated against it every 24 hours; a new subscription can need up to 48 hours before budgets work.
Budgets at subscription or resource group scope can call an action group, which can trigger automation such as Functions or webhooks.
Resource locks and backup data must be removed before a resource group can be deleted.

Resource Manager deletes nested resources first, then resources that manage others (managedBy), then the rest, waiting for dependencies; a delete is retried for 5xx, 429 and 408 for 15 minutes by default; a 404 on GET means success.

documentedSources.title: Use tags to organize your Azure resources

claims.text: Resources do not inherit tags applied to a resource group or subscription.
At most 50 tag name-value pairs per resource, group or subscription; tag names up to 512 characters (128 for storage accounts), values up to 256; tag values are case-sensitive.

documentedSources.title: Delete and recover a Log Analytics workspace

claims.text: Deleting a workspace soft-deletes it for 14 days and the name stays reserved; a workspace already in the soft-delete state must be recovered before it can be permanently removed; the --force parameter of the workspace delete command makes the deletion permanent (command group: az monitor log-analytics workspace).

documentedSources.title: Set daily cap on a Log Analytics workspace

claims.text: The daily cap cannot stop collection at exactly the cap and some excess data is expected; data collected above the cap is still billed; the reset hour cannot be configured.

documentedSources.title: az webapp deployment slot (Azure CLI reference)

claims.text: az webapp deployment slot swap --slot <slot> [--name] [--resource-group] [--subscription] [--target-slot] [--action {preview, reset, swap}]; the default action is swap and the default target slot is production.
--action preview applies the target slot's settings on the source slot first; --action swap completes it; --action reset resets the swap.
The delete form of the az webapp deployment slot group takes --slot <slot> [--name] [--resource-group] [--subscription] and removes a deployment slot.

documentedSources.title: az monitor log-analytics workspace (Azure CLI reference)

claims.text: az monitor log-analytics workspace list-deleted-workspaces gets a list of deleted workspaces that can be recovered in a subscription or a resource group (Core, GA).
az graph query -q <query> [--subscriptions] queries the resources managed by Azure Resource Manager; it is an extension command (GA).
az deployment sub validate validates whether a template is valid at subscription scope and az deployment sub what-if executes a what-if operation at subscription scope (both Core, GA).

The required --location (-l) parameter of az deployment sub validate is described as the location to store the deployment metadata (read on Learn 2026-11-06); it is not described as the region of the resources, which come from the template and its parameters.
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName <string> -Action <CimInstance[]> [-Description] [-Settings] [-Trigger]; the page example creates the trigger with New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -At 12:00 -Once.

New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet accepts -AllowStartIfOnBatteries, -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries, -StartWhenAvailable, -WakeToRun and -ExecutionTimeLimit <TimeSpan>; Unregister-ScheduledTask accepts -TaskName and -Confirm.

teardown.rule: The deadline is an absolute UTC time written to the tag lease-expires-utc when the resource group is created; the teardown job is registered before that moment and before any billable resource.
teardown.default: Owner-machine one-shot scheduled job (Windows Task Scheduler, registered by arming step 5) that runs the teardown script below at lease-expires-utc with the owner az session; no Azure resource and no Azure cost (estimated).
teardown.automaticBackstopFirstAction: After guards G2 and G3, the first action of the automatic backstop is the deletion of the slot, the web app and the plan; it exports nothing and waits for nothing.

job.name: ass-teardown-<lease-id>
script: if ((az account show --query id -o tsv) -ne $Subscription) { throw 'G2: the az session selects another subscription than the approved one' }
if (-not $g -or $g.name -ine $Group -or $g.tags.'lease-id' -cne $Lease -or -not $g.tags.'lease-expires-utc') { throw 'G3: group name or lease tags differ from this lease' }
try { Assert-Subscription; if ((az group exists --name $Group --subscription $Subscription) -eq 'false') { exit 0 } } catch { $failures.Add("first check: $($_.Exception.Message)") }

try { Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az webapp deployment slot delete --resource-group $Group --name $App --slot staging --subscription $Subscription } catch { $failures.Add("slot: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
try { Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az webapp delete --resource-group $Group --name $App --subscription $Subscription } catch { $failures.Add("web app: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
try { Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az appservice plan delete --resource-group $Group --name $Plan --yes --subscription $Subscription } catch { $failures.Add("plan: $($_.Exception.Message)") }

if ($Workspace) { try { Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az monitor log-analytics workspace delete --resource-group $Group --workspace-name $Workspace --force --yes --subscription $Subscription } catch { $failures.Add("workspace: $($_.Exception.Message)") } }
try { Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az group delete --name $Group --yes --subscription $Subscription } catch { $failures.Add("group: $($_.Exception.Message)") }

try { Assert-Subscription; if ((az group exists --name $Group --subscription $Subscription) -ne 'false') { $failures.Add('the group still exists after its delete') } } catch { $failures.Add("final check: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
$m = "TEARDOWN FAILED for lease ${Lease} ($($failures.Count) problems): $($failures -join ' | '). The meter may still run: delete the lease by hand now (deletion order of the packet)."
try { Set-Content -Path $alarmFile -Value $m; $m += " The same text is in the file $alarmFile." } catch { $m += ' (the alarm file could not be written: this dialog is the only alarm)' }
job.onGuardFailure: Each delete is wrapped: a failing guard or delete is recorded, the script continues, always finishes with the guarded group delete (it removes everything) when the group guard still passes, verifies that the group is gone, and on any problem writes a persistent alarm file in the Desktop folder reported by Windows (it may be redirected: when that folder does not exist the script uses the temp folder, then the script folder), shows a dialog that names the file or says that it could not be written, and exits 1.

backstops: Cost Management budget on the lease resource group at 50, 80 and 100 percent of the spend ceiling (planning bound, not enforced by Azure) with email; alert only, evaluated every 24 hours on data that lags 8 to 24 hours (documented, BUDGET-ALERTONLY and BUDGET-LAG), so it cannot enforce a short-run ceiling.
Owner check at deadline plus 1 hour using verification checks 1 and 2.
Stop rule on scale: no autoscale rules, manual instance count only, and the instance cap of the option is the most the plan may ever be set to.
teardown.notSelected: Azure-side automation (Automation account, Logic App, Function with an identity and a role assignment) would be more robust against an offline workstation but adds resources and an identity: price unavailable (not queried), excluded.
limits: The job runs only while the owner machine is on (WakeToRun and StartWhenAvailable help only if the operating system allows wake timers), the owner is logged on (the task runs as the interactive user) and the az session is still valid at the deadline.

If the machine stays off or the session is invalid, nothing is deleted and no alarm is raised at all: the owner check at deadline plus 1 hour (verification checks 1 and 2) is then the only control, and the manual deletion block below is the fallback.

The alarm file and the dialog appear only when the script runs; the file stays until the owner removes it. It is written to the Desktop folder reported by Windows (it may be redirected), else to the temp folder, else to the script folder; the dialog names the file or says that it could not be written. The dialog is closed by the 2-hour execution limit.

deletionOrder.step: Define the variables and the guard functions (paste first; PowerShell 7.4 or later)
commands: if ((az account show --query id -o tsv) -ne $Subscription) { throw 'G2: the az session selects another subscription than the approved one' }
if (-not $g -or $g.name -ine $Group -or $g.tags.'lease-id' -cne $Lease -or -not $g.tags.'lease-expires-utc') { throw 'G3: group name or lease tags differ from this lease' }
deletionOrder.label: estimated
deletionOrder.why: Every delete line below calls Assert-Subscription (G2) and Assert-Lease (G3) itself, so copying only this code block keeps every delete guarded; a failed guard throws and the rest of that line does not run.

deletionOrder.step: Stop the meter: delete the slot, the web app, then the App Service plan (the first action of the automatic backstop)
commands: Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az webapp deployment slot delete --resource-group $Group --name $App --slot staging --subscription $Subscription
Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az appservice plan delete --resource-group $Group --name $Plan --yes --subscription $Subscription
deletionOrder.label: estimated
deletionOrder.why: The plan is the only fixed-rate meter and each plan instance is billed (documented, PLANS-BILLING); an empty plan keeps its instances, so it must be deleted explicitly. Each of the three lines runs G2 and G3 first.

deletionOrder.step: Delete observability (B and C): Application Insights, diagnostic settings, then the workspace permanently
commands: Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az monitor log-analytics workspace delete --resource-group $Group --workspace-name $Workspace --force --yes --subscription $Subscription
deletionOrder.label: documented
deletionOrder.why: Without --force the workspace is only soft-deleted for 14 days and its name stays reserved (documented, LADEL-SOFT). Guards run first.

deletionOrder.step: Delete the storage account after the evidence export
commands: Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az storage account delete --resource-group $Group --name $Storage --yes --subscription $Subscription
deletionOrder.label: estimated
deletionOrder.why: Stops capacity and operation charges; the manual path confirms the export hash first, the backstop skips this step because step 5 deletes the account with the group.

deletionOrder.step: Delete lease identities (only if identityRegistration was yes)
commands: Assert-Subscription; Assert-Lease; az role assignment delete --assignee <identity-principal-id> --scope "/subscriptions/$Subscription/resourceGroups/$Group/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/$Storage" --subscription $Subscription
deletionOrder.label: estimated
deletionOrder.why: Only a user-assigned managed identity inside the lease group is allowed; its role assignments are scoped to the lease storage account and are removed first. Nothing may exist at subscription scope.

deletionOrder.step: Catch-all: delete the lease resource group
deletionOrder.label: documented
deletionOrder.why: Resource Manager deletes nested, then managedBy, then remaining resources and retries transient errors for 15 minutes; locks and backup data must not exist (documented, RGDEL-PRECOND and RGDEL-ORDER); this plan creates none. --yes is used only after G2 and G3 passed on the same line; without --no-wait the command returns only when the deletion finished, so a failure is seen.

deletionOrder.step: Disarm the scheduled teardown job: NOT part of the pasted block; run it by hand as the first command of verification check 6 in section 4.5, only after checks 1 to 4 passed
deletionOrder.label: documented
deletionOrder.why: A disarmed job with a failed verification would leave nothing watching the lease, and a pasted block that ended with the disarm would remove the only automatic backstop when a host keeps running after a failed line. The disarm line of check 6 also refuses to run while az group exists does not answer false.

verification.check: The lease resource group is gone
commands: foreach ($i in 1..12) { if ((az group exists --name <rg> --subscription <subscription-id>) -eq 'false') { 'gone'; break }; Start-Sleep -Seconds 300 }
verification.expect: the first command prints <subscription-id> and the loop prints gone within 60 minutes; if the group still exists, G3 runs before any further delete

verification.check: No lease resource remains anywhere in the subscription (G2 first)

az graph query -q "resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups' and name =~ '<rg>' | project id" --subscriptions <subscription-id>
verification.expect: the first command prints <subscription-id> (G2); 0 rows for both queries; repeat after 15 minutes and next day because Resource Graph is eventually consistent. The extension is a one-time local install on the owner machine.

verification.check: No soft-deleted workspace keeps the lease name reserved
commands: az monitor log-analytics workspace list-deleted-workspaces --subscription <subscription-id> --query "[?name=='<law>'].id" -o tsv
verification.expect: the first command prints <subscription-id> (G2); empty output; the workspace was deleted with --force (command form on Learn, DOC-CLI-LADELETED)

verification.check: No identity or role assignment created for the lease remains
commands: az graph query -q "resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.managedidentity/userassignedidentities' and tags['lease-id'] == '<lease-id>' | project id" --subscriptions <subscription-id>
verification.expect: the first command prints <subscription-id> (G2); 0 rows and empty output; record not applicable for the identity when identityRegistration was no (the queries still run). Entra app registrations and service principals are forbidden by this packet and are not searched.
verification.label: estimated

verification.check: Spend stayed within the ceiling and stopped at the deadline
verification.portal: Portal: Cost Management > Cost analysis > scope = the subscription > filter Tag lease-id = <lease-id> > the lease day and the next day; read the budget alert mails
verification.expect: total at or below the approved ceiling and no cost on later days; cost data lags 8 to 24 hours (documented, BUDGET-LAG)
verification.label: documented

verification.check: The job is disarmed (only after checks 1 to 4 passed) and the lease record is closed
commands: if ((az group exists --name $Group --subscription $Subscription) -eq 'false') { Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'ass-teardown-<lease-id>' -Confirm:$false } else { throw 'the group still exists: the backstop stays armed' }
verification.expect: The first command disarms the job only when az group exists answers false and throws (the backstop stays armed) otherwise; run it in the PowerShell session of the deletion block, where $Group and $Subscription are set. Get-ScheduledTask then prints nothing; the record holds lease id, option, start and end UTC, every verification output and the evidence hash

rollback.when: Code deployment or startup fails in the staging slot
rollback.label: documented
rollback.action: Production was never touched: the target slot stays online while the source slot is prepared (documented, SLOTS-TARGET-ONLINE). Fix and redeploy the staging slot, or delete the slot content; no swap happened, so nothing is rolled back.

rollback.when: A swap completed but post-swap checks fail
commands: az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app> --slot staging --target-slot production --subscription <subscription-id>
rollback.label: documented
rollback.action: Run G2 and G3, then swap the same two slots again immediately to restore the pre-swap states (documented, SLOTS-ROLLBACK; command form on Learn, DOC-CLI-SLOTSWAP). Expect the former production workers to be recycled in each swap (documented, SLOTS-RECYCLE) and record both swap timings.

rollback.when: First swap of a fresh app
rollback.label: documented
commands: az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app> --slot staging --target-slot production --subscription <subscription-id> --action preview
az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app> --slot staging --target-slot production --subscription <subscription-id> --action swap
az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app> --slot staging --target-slot production --subscription <subscription-id> --action reset
rollback.action: Use swap with preview after G2 and G3: the first command applies the production slot settings to staging so the staging slot can be validated, the second completes the swap, the third cancels the preview (documented, SLOTS-PREVIEW and CLI-SWAP-ACTIONS).

rollback.when: Warm-up could mask a broken app
rollback.label: documented
rollback.action: Set WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_PATH to a health path and WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_STATUSES to an explicit list such as 200, because the default accepts any HTTP response (documented, SLOTS-WARMUP).

rollback.when: Someone proposes auto swap for the Linux app
rollback.label: documented
rollback.action: Do not configure it: auto swap is not supported on Linux (documented, SLOTS-NOAUTOSWAP); every swap is an explicit command.

rollback.when: The first-ever deployment has no previous version
rollback.label: estimated
rollback.action: Production holds only the platform placeholder, so there is nothing to swap back to: do not swap; delete and recreate the slot or the lease and rerun.

rollback.label: estimated
rollback.action: Incremental deployments can leave partial resources. Do not hand-patch: run the teardown (guards G2 and G3, then the deletion order) and redeploy under a new lease id. ARM rollback-on-error is not relied on.

rollback.when: The teardown job does not run, or a delete fails or hangs
rollback.label: documented
rollback.action: Run G2 and G3, delete the plan explicitly first to stop the meter, then repeat the group deletion (deletion order step 5); if a lock exists remove it first (documented, RGDEL-PRECOND; this plan creates none). If a guard fails, do not delete: tell the owner. The budget email is only a late backstop (documented, BUDGET-LAG).

guards.name: Pre-creation gate
guards.onFailure: STOP. A group with this name already exists: do not create, tag, reuse or delete it; tell the owner and choose a new name.

guards.name: Subscription pin
guards.expect: prints exactly the approved <subscription-id>. It is the only az command without --subscription because it reads the session default on purpose. Every other az command of the lease, of the scheduled job and of the checks carries --subscription <subscription-id> (az graph query carries --subscriptions <subscription-id>). In scripts and in the manual deletion block this guard is the function Assert-Subscription.
guards.onFailure: ABORT before any other command and tell the owner.

guards.name: Ownership check before EACH delete
guards.expect: name equals <rg> (case-insensitive), tag lease-id equals <lease-id> exactly, and tag lease-expires-utc is present. In scripts and in the manual deletion block this guard is the function Assert-Lease, called on the same line before each delete.
guards.onFailure: ABORT this delete and every later one and tell the owner; nothing is deleted on a mismatch.

guards.name: The same guards inside verification checks 1 to 4
guards.expect: checks 1 to 4 start with the subscription pin (G2) as their first command; while check 1 still sees the group, the ownership check G3 runs before any further deletion
guards.onFailure: a mismatch aborts the check and is reported to the owner.

armingSequence.step: Quota and policy gate: a non-deploying validation and what-if with the template parameters set to the chosen region AND SKU
armingSequence.expect: both succeed. --location only stores the deployment metadata (documented, CLI-DEPLOY-LOCATION); the region and SKU that are validated come from the template and its parameters, so the parameters must set <region> and the SKU of the chosen option (<sku>); the owner defaults of the reviewed template (centralus, P1v3: the combination that failed on 5 Nov) must not be used unless that is the chosen option. Read the resolved location and SKU in the what-if output before continuing. Any error, including InternalSubscriptionIsOverQuotaForSku, means STOP: pick another candidate region or have the quota raised, and repeat this step. Do not start while an earlier subscription-scope deployment is still running. Decide before arming which side creates the group: step 6 (script) or the reviewed template, never both (a template that also declares the group would meet the tagged group of step 6).
armingSequence.label: documented

armingSequence.expect: the value (UTC, culture-invariant: the same text under fi-FI, da-DK, th-TH and ar-SA) is written to tag lease-expires-utc in step 6
armingSequence.label: estimated

armingSequence.step: Register the one-shot teardown job BEFORE any billable resource (Windows Task Scheduler, PowerShell 7.4 or later)
commands: Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'ass-teardown-<lease-id>' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -Description 'Backstop: delete lease <lease-id> at its deadline'

if ([Math]::Abs(($registered - [DateTimeOffset]::Parse($expires, [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture).UtcDateTime).TotalSeconds) -gt 120) { throw 'the registered trigger time differs from the deadline: unregister the task and start again' }
armingSequence.expect: Get-ScheduledTask prints the task with State Ready, the line "registered trigger (UTC)" shows the time the task will fire and equals the deadline printed next to it (the last command throws when they differ by more than 2 minutes); the script it runs is listed below and carries guards G2 and G3. The app, plan and (B and C) workspace names are the ones of the lease.

armingSequence.step: Create the resource group with the lease tags
commands: az group create --name <rg> --location <region> --subscription <subscription-id> --tags lease-id=<lease-id> lease-owner=<owner-alias> "lease-expires-utc=$expires" purpose=native-proof-first-code-slot card=C062 option=<option-letter> cost-ceiling-usd=<5|15|75>
armingSequence.label: documented

armingSequence.step: Check the tags before anything else is created (G3)
armingSequence.expect: name, lease-id and lease-expires-utc are as written in step 6
armingSequence.label: documented

armingSequence.step: Budget on the group (optional, alert only)
armingSequence.expect: created by the reviewed Bicep (Microsoft.Consumption/budgets) or in the portal; never a control (documented, BUDGET-ALERTONLY)
armingSequence.label: documented

armingSequence.step: Create the resources through the reviewed IaC, tagging every resource
armingSequence.expect: every resource shows the seven lease tags (tags are not inherited)
armingSequence.label: documented

manualBeforeDeletion.step: Export evidence (manual path only, before the deadline)
manualBeforeDeletion.action: Stop issuing commands; export run logs, Table, Queue and Blob contents and App Service logs to the owner machine; record the SHA-256 of the export.
manualBeforeDeletion.rule: The automatic backstop never exports and never waits for an export: its first action is the deletion. Evidence that is not exported before the deadline is lost by design.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Deployment slots need the Standard, Premium or Isolated tier. Basic (B1 from $0.017 per hour) and Free are cheaper but have no slots and are excluded; Standard allows 5 slots and Premium 20, so one staging slot fits every option.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Slots cost nothing extra and run on the plan instances, so swap overlap needs spare capacity on the same instances; the plan instance-hour is the only fixed-rate meter.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Auto swap is unavailable on Linux, so every swap and rollback is an explicit command; rollback is the same swap repeated at once.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: The default warm-up accepts any HTTP response and swaps recycle the former production workers, abandoning long operations: set strict warm-up statuses and keep the proof app fault tolerant.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Node.js 24 LTS on Linux App Service is documented as NODE|24-lts. Production-runtime validation is still unperformed (approvals.C001: Node 22.23.4 is test tooling only).

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Cost Management cannot enforce a ceiling on a run of hours: budgets only notify, on data 8 to 24 hours old. The ceiling (planning bound, not enforced by Azure) comes from price times capped instances times the teardown deadline plus one latency hour, and holds only if the scheduled teardown runs (R16).

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Lease tags must be written on every resource explicitly; the group tag is not inherited. Seven tags are far below the 50-tag limit.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: A workspace deleted without --force stays soft-deleted for 14 days with its name reserved, and the daily cap can be exceeded and the excess is billed: the log lines of B and C are bounded estimates, not guarantees.

risksAndAssumptions.label: documented
risksAndAssumptions.text: Premium v4 is cheaper (P0v4 $0.073 per hour in eastus2 against $0.0775 for P0v3) and offered in all five candidate regions, but it has no stable outbound IPs, availability depends on the resource group deployment unit, and its slot count is not stated on its page. It is listed as an alternative, not selected.

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: P0v3, P1 v3 and P2 v3 support slots because they are in the Premium tier (documented by tier, not by SKU name). The first what-if or create call is the real check.

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: Prices are retail pay-as-you-go list prices in USD returned on 2026-11-04. Billed prices can differ (discounts, taxes, currency) and change; the packet is stale after 7 days (planning assumption).

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: Monthly figures use 730 hours per month. Ceilings assume billing in whole started hours plus one teardown-latency hour at the instance cap (the time between the deadline and the plan actually being deleted), which is conservative if billing is finer.

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: Run windows (3, 6 and 24 hours) and usage caps are planning assumptions that the test harness must enforce, not Azure; exceeding a cap means stop and tear down.

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: The API returns zero-priced first tiers (Log Analytics first 5 GB, egress first 100 GB). They are explicit returned values, not missing prices, but the ceilings do not rely on them: every GB is priced at the paid tier.

risksAndAssumptions.label: estimated
risksAndAssumptions.text: The default teardown job needs the owner machine on (the task settings wake it and start it when available), the az session valid and the approved subscription selected at the deadline. If a guard fails the job deletes nothing, shows a dialog and exits 1; if the job never runs the exposure is the per-hour cost until someone tears down by hand, and the budget mail arrives a day later.

risksAndAssumptions.text: HEAD holds the owner native demo (demo/, infra/, the azure-demo workflows, demo/cleanup.cjs and .azure/deployment-plan.md, commit f42f4e03). None of it is an approval or part of this packet lease, and this packet defers to the owner plan for the concrete target (section 0a). Revision 4 fixes all three. No price, ceiling, decision or approval changed.
revision.pricesKept: All 116 unit prices stay unchanged (re-confirmed by independent lookups on 2026-11-06, no difference since 2026-11-04) and stay usable until 2026-11-11 by the 7-day rule (R11).

changes.change: The teardown script resolves the alarm folder with [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop') (the Desktop folder reported by Windows, which may be redirected), falls back to the temp folder and then to the script folder when that folder does not exist, and its dialog names the alarm file or says that it could not be written. Revision 3 built the path by hand and wrote no file on a machine whose Desktop is redirected.

The disarm of the scheduled job (Unregister-ScheduledTask) is no longer the last line of the pasted deletion block: it is the first command of verification check 6 in section 4.5, after the four verifications, and it runs only when az group exists answers false (otherwise it throws and the backstop stays armed).
Appendix D says that the validator refuses the listed shapes, is a tripwire for accidental edits and not a proof, and points to its README for the covered and the uncovered spellings.

earlier.reason: The independent review of 2026-11-06 found revision 2 sound (prices, arithmetic and guards re-verified) and listed seven minor packet findings, A1 to A7, about money safety and precision. Revision 3 fixes all of them. No price, ceiling, decision or approval changed.

changes.change: Arming step 3 sets the template parameters for the region AND the SKU (--location only stores the deployment metadata), tells the owner to read the resolved location and SKU in the what-if output, names the owner defaults that failed on 5 Nov, decides who creates the group and warns about a running subscription-scope deployment.
Every timestamp is built and parsed with InvariantCulture (the former text broke under fi-FI and da-DK and set the year 2569 or 1448 under th-TH and ar-SA).
The registration check prints the registered trigger time and compares it with the deadline; the last command throws on a difference of more than 2 minutes.

The unattended teardown wraps every delete, never stops at the first failure, always finishes with the guarded group delete and a check that the group is gone, records every failure, exits 1 and raises a persistent alarm file plus the dialog (revision 3 built the Desktop path by hand and wrote no file on a machine whose Desktop is redirected: corrected in revision 4, N1); what it cannot guarantee when the machine is off is stated.
The manual deletion block carries the guard functions and every delete line calls Assert-Subscription (G2) and Assert-Lease (G3) itself, so copying only the code block stays guarded.
The list and create-container meter sentence names the regions where the meter IDs are equal and where only the price is equal; the deadline rule says the time arming step 4 computes.
The ceiling headroom (B about 1.9 and C about 3.85 at-cap hours before the next step) is stated next to the ceilings and recomputed by the validator.
Appendix D no longer claims that any GUID, e-mail or secret is rejected: it names the validator README for the covered and the uncovered spellings.
